amigues: Suzanne Amigues, “Le silphium — État de la question,” Journal des Savants (2004), 191–226.
A close study of ancient evidence for the plant's range, identification, and later testimony.
briggs: Lisa Briggs and Jens Jakobsson, “Searching for Silphium: An Updated Review,” Heritage 5 (2022), 936–955.
Surveys the sources, material evidence, trade, and proposed botanical identifications.
parejko: Ken Parejko, “Pliny the Elder’s Silphium: First Recorded Species Extinction,” Conservation Biology 17 (2003), 925–927.
Reads Pliny's scarcity report as a possible account of human-driven extinction.
roques: Denis Roques, “Synésios de Cyrène et le Silphion de Cyrénaïque,” Revue des Études Grecques 97 (1984), 218–231.
A study focused on Synesius's letters and the problem of late silphium testimony.

palsson: Gísli Pálsson, The Last of Its Kind
thomas: Jessica E. Thomas et al., “Demographic reconstruction”
lucas: Frederic A. Lucas, The Expedition to Funk Island
birkhead: Tim R. Birkhead and Peter T. Gallivan, “Alfred Newton’s contribution to ornithology”

strickland-clusius: Hugh Edwin Strickland and Alexander Gordon Melville, The Dodo and Its Kindred (1848), pp. 12–17, 125.
strickland-herbert: Hugh Edwin Strickland and Alexander Gordon Melville, The Dodo and Its Kindred (1848), pp. 19–21.
strickland-lestrange: Hugh Edwin Strickland and Alexander Gordon Melville, The Dodo and Its Kindred (1848), pp. 22–23.
strickland-cauche: Hugh Edwin Strickland and Alexander Gordon Melville, The Dodo and Its Kindred (1848), pp. 21–22, 125–126.

husson-holthuis: A. M. Husson and L. B. Holthuis, “The earliest figures of the Blaauwbok, Hippotragus leucophaeus (Pallas, 1766) and of the Greater Kudu, Tragelaphus strepsiceros (Pallas, 1766)” (1975), Zoologische Mededelingen 49(5): 57–63.
Early descriptions and illustrations, including Pennant’s 1771 account.
rookmaaker: L. C. Rookmaaker, The Zoological Exploration of Southern Africa 1650–1790 (1989), species account 49, pp. 300–301.
Rotterdam and Brookfield: A. A. Balkema. Historical records of the bluebuck.
hempel: Elisabeth Hempel et al., “Identifying the true number of specimens of the extinct blue antelope (Hippotragus leucophaeus)” (2021), Scientific Reports 11: 2100.
Historical distribution, extinction, and identification of museum specimens. DOI: 10.1038/s41598-020-80142-2.

castaways: Jane Cameron National Archives, Archives Newsletter 8 (2020), “Castaways.”
Reproduces Tyssen’s account of the rescue.
blair: James J. A. Blair, Salvaging Empire: Sovereignty, Natural Resources, and Environmental Science in the South Atlantic (Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 2023).
Cites the October 1894 Falkland Islands Magazine.

royster: Georg Wilhelm Steller, De Bestiis Marinis, or, The Beasts of the Sea (1751), trans. Walter Miller and Jennie Emerson Miller, ed. Paul Royster (2011).
Lincoln: University of Nebraska–Lincoln Libraries. Edited online text of the 1899 translation.
turvey-risley: Samuel T. Turvey and Claire L. Risley, “Modelling the extinction of Steller’s sea cow” (2006), Biology Letters 2(1): 94–97.
Estimates of the population and hunting pressure after 1741. DOI: 10.1098/rsbl.2005.0415.
stejneger-1886: Leonhard Stejneger, “On the Extermination of the Great Northern Sea-Cow (Rytina): A Reply to Professor A. E. Nordenskiöld” (1886), Journal of the American Geographical Society of New York 18: 317–328.
Stejneger’s re-examination of Nordenskiöld’s informants on Bering Island.
stejneger-1887: Leonhard Stejneger, “How the Great Northern Sea-Cow (Rytina) Became Exterminated” (1887), American Naturalist 21(12): 1047–1054.
Hunting parties on the Commander Islands after 1742, Jakovlev’s petition of 1755, and the 1768 date.

oliver: S. Pasfield Oliver, ed., The Voyage of François Leguat of Bresse to Rodriguez, Mauritius, Java, and the Cape of Good Hope (1891), 2 vols.
London: Hakluyt Society. Annotated reprint of the 1708 English text, with the Relation de l’île Rodrigue in Appendix B.
strickland: H. E. Strickland and A. G. Melville, The Dodo and Its Kindred (1848), “The Brevipennate Bird of Rodriguez, the Solitaire,” pp. 46–56.
London: Reeve, Benham, and Reeve. Early comparison of Leguat with other accounts.
newton-1869: Alfred Newton and Edward Newton, “On the Osteology of the Solitaire or Didine Bird of the Island of Rodriguez, Pezophaps solitaria (Gmel.)” (1869), Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society 159: 327–362.
Subfossil skeletons compared with Leguat’s description. DOI: 10.1098/rstl.1869.0011.
hume-steel: Julian P. Hume and Lorna Steel, “Fight club: a unique weapon in the wing of the solitaire, Pezophaps solitaria” (2013), Biological Journal of the Linnean Society 110: 32–44.
The carpal knob described by Leguat. DOI: 10.1111/bij.12087.
